paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Hezekiah was lifted up by the LORD, and a proud heart is what tripped him. The text says that "because his heart was proud, Hezekiah did not repay the favor shown to him" (2 Chronicles 32:25). Pride is sneaky like that. It doesn't announce itself. It just quietly stops you from saying thank you.

But look at the turn, baker. "Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart—he and the people of Jerusalem" (2 Chronicles 32:26). Humbling yourself is something you can do, and it matters. It doesn't keep a heart from ever being tested, though. When the ambassadors from Babylon came, "God left him alone to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah's heart" (2 Chronicles 32:31). Good things don't prove a heart is steady, and a test shows what's in it.

So what do you do with that? You thank the One who gave you the good things, and you keep your heart low when they pile up. I think that's easy to say and hard to do, and I bet Hezekiah would nod along. The story isn't over, though. Hezekiah's son Manasseh takes the throne (2 Chronicles 32:33), and there's more to come.
